gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a Google TV projector can't read a USB drive until you install a file manager from the Play Store. Nebula says this is because 'Google's policy prohibits pre-installing file managers.' Google's own help page says the offline 'basic TV' setup can't install apps or receive casts, so a Google TV projector that never goes online can't play a USB stick or take a cast.
standout_why: I compared these pages: innovativeprojector.com says only that 'a few models push users through an online activation process, account login, or software update' and that streaming services 'may block certain forms of screen mirroring', without naming Google TV or explaining why. nexttools.net says AirPlay, Miracast and Chromecast need Wi-Fi infrastructure and nothing about setup or USB apps. The Laser Corporation FAQ covers USB codecs (H.264 MP4/AVI/MOV, drives up to 128 GB) for its own non-Google-TV unit only. None of them says that Google TV can't read USB without a file manager it has to download, or that offline basic TV can't install apps. ChatGPT's answer says 'USB projector: play videos directly from a USB flash drive' without that limit.
decides: If the shopper truly has no Wi-Fi and wants to play movies from a USB drive, a Google TV projector is the wrong pick unless they can get it online once. That covers Dealectric's NEBULA Capsule 3 GTV and possibly the XGIMI MoGo 4, Aurzen BOOM mini and Aurzen EAZZE D1 MAX. A phone hotspot works: finish full Google TV setup, install a file manager and VLC, MX Player or Kodi, then go offline. With basic TV you get HDMI only: no app installs and no casting. For a never-online plan, pick a projector with no smart OS and a built-in media player. Or, for a phone source, use a wired or peer-to-peer link such as the Aurzen ZIP projectors with the CastPlay Pro dongle. That needs no network, but only if the phone's USB-C port supports DisplayPort Alt Mode.

findings.label: Google TV basic TV: what it can do offline
findings.value: Basic TV can be set up without a Google Account or an internet connection. It can't install apps, use Play Library, use Assistant content search, use sign-in services, or receive casts from another device.
findings.source_title: Google TV Help: Use basic TV
findings.note: Google's page: 'You can only use basic TV on TVs that come with Google TV built in.' It doesn't mention projectors, so whether each projector offers basic TV during setup isn't confirmed. Once Google TV is fully set up, you can't switch to basic TV without a factory reset. Google warns: 'Without an internet connection, your device won't get important security updates.'

findings.label: USB playback needs a downloaded file manager (Nebula Google TV projectors)
findings.value: 'Before using a USB flash drive, you must install a file manager.' 'Google's policy prohibits pre-installing file managers on the system.' 'Without a file manager, the projector will not be able to read files from the USB storage device.'
findings.source_title: How Do I Play Files From My USB Drive with Projector? (soundcore/Nebula support)
findings.note: The article covers Nebula's Google TV projectors in general and names no single model. It recommends Nebula File Manager plus VLC, MX Player or Kodi. Only FAT32 and NTFS are fully supported; on exFAT only MX Player plays files. The 'Google policy' wording is Nebula's; I didn't find Google's own policy text.

findings.label: Nebula's 'play videos without Wi-Fi' steps include a Play Store install
findings.value: Steps: download videos to a USB drive; 'Install the File Explorer app from the Google Play Store'; install a media player app; connect the USB drive and play. Supports drives up to 4 TB, FAT32 and NTFS only.
findings.source_title: How do I play videos without Wi-Fi? (soundcore/Nebula support)
findings.note: The article names Capsule 3 Laser for the File Explorer step. Even Nebula's 'without Wi-Fi' guide relies on a Play Store install, which needs internet at least once.

findings.label: Video inputs per maker spec
findings.value: One HDMI 2.1/ARC video input. USB-C is listed only as power input (PD 20 V / 2.25 A).
findings.source_title: soundcore Nebula Capsule 3 | 1080p Mini Google TV Projector
findings.note: The spec lists the OS as 'Android TV 11.0', but the title says Google TV. The page doesn't mention USB media playback.

findings.label: Network-free phone link via CastPlay Pro dongle
findings.value: 'CastPlay Pro uses a direct peer-to-peer connection, so there's no need for Wi-Fi, network setup, or additional apps.' It needs the phone's USB-C port to support DisplayPort Alt Mode video output. Aurzen says it supports DRM-protected streaming such as Netflix and Disney+.
findings.source_title: Aurzen CastPlay Pro Wireless USB-C Dongle Help Center
findings.note: If no picture appears, Aurzen says this 'nearly always means your phone's USB-C port does not support DisplayPort Alternate Mode (DP Alt Mode) video output' and calls it a phone hardware limit. Aurzen guarantees Samsung Galaxy S/Note/Z (S8 and newer), and the FAQ also mentions iPhone, iPad, MacBook and Switch in general. Pixel is listed only as a model to check. The page says the dongle casts 'directly to your ZIP projector' but doesn't list compatible ZIP models one by one. The dongle is sold separately.
